beginnerNote: Light, friendly and predictable for a 755cc twin, and the A2 version makes it legally accessible - but 92 PS and a sharp throttle are a lot for a true first bike.
whoFor: Riders stepping up to their first big bike who want serious pace, agile handling and modern electronics without a big price tag.
notFor: Maybe not for you if you regularly ride long motorway distances two-up - there is little wind protection and the pillion perch is compact.
about: The CB750 Hornet is Honda's mid-size streetfighter, built around a punchy 755cc 270-degree parallel twin with a class-leading power-to-weight ratio (192 kg wet, 67.5 kW). The 2025 facelift brought a low-set dual LED projector headlight, a five-inch TFT with Honda RoadSync connectivity and retuned Showa suspension. It rides light, flickable and eager, with riding modes, traction and wheelie control managed by throttle-by-wire.
pros: Class-leading power-to-weight ratio (0.36 kW/kg)
Torquey, characterful 270-degree twin
Low 795 mm seat and light 192 kg wet weight
Strong value for money
2025 update adds TFT display and distinctive LED face
cons: Almost no wind protection for motorway work
Suspension is budget-oriented with limited adjustability
sources: Honda Motor Europe 25YM CB750 Hornet press kit technical specifications (hondanews.eu)

beginnerNote: Smooth power delivery, neutral handling and an A2 option make it approachable, but the 850 mm seat and 210 kg are a handful for shorter or completely new riders.
whoFor: Riders who want one do-it-all adventure bike for commuting, two-up touring and genuine gravel-road capability without flagship-adventure weight or cost.
notFor: Maybe not for you if you want serious hard-enduro ability or premium touring kit like cruise control out of the box.
about: The XL750 Transalp pairs the CB750 Hornet's 755cc twin with a 21/18-inch spoked-wheel adventure chassis and long-travel Showa suspension. The 2025 facelift added an Africa Twin-style face with dual projector LED headlight, a new five-inch TFT with RoadSync, and retuned damping developed on European roads. It is a composed, easy-going all-rounder that handles light off-road confidently while staying comfortable on the road.
pros: Flexible, economical 755cc twin (4.3 L/100km, ~390 km range)
Long-travel suspension and 21-inch front handle real gravel
Five riding modes incl. Gravel, plus deactivatable rear ABS
Comfortable ergonomics with strong two-up ability
2025 update improved lighting, screen and suspension
cons: Tube-type tyres complicate roadside puncture repair
No cruise control even as an option
Basic axial two-piston front brake calipers
850 mm seat is tall for shorter riders
sources: Honda Motor Europe 25YM XL750 Transalp press kit technical specifications (hondanews.eu)

beginnerNote: Featherweight, forgiving and cheap to run - one of the friendliest ways into motorcycling, provided you can manage the tall 880 mm dirt-bike seat.
whoFor: New riders and trail-curious commuters who want a light, unbreakable dual-sport that is as happy on forest tracks as in city traffic.
notFor: Maybe not for you if your riding involves sustained motorway speeds or regular two-up trips.
about: The CRF300L is Honda's lightweight dual-sport: a 286cc single with a six-speed gearbox and slipper clutch in a slim 142 kg package with 285 mm of ground clearance and long-travel suspension. The 2025 update brought LED lighting, improved heat management and Euro5+ compliance. It is slow by road-bike standards but nearly indestructible, sips fuel at 3.1 L/100km, and its 21/18-inch wheels shrug off terrain that would stop most road bikes.
pros: Just 142 kg kerb weight - easy to handle and pick up
Genuine off-road ability with 285 mm ground clearance
Very cheap to buy, run and insure
Frugal 3.1 L/100km gives ~250 km from the small tank
Natively A2 compliant
cons: 27 PS means motorway cruising is strained
880 mm seat height challenges shorter riders
Small 7.8 L tank limits touring range
Basic LCD dash and minimal wind protection
sources: Honda Motor Europe 25YM CRF300L press kit technical specifications (hondanews.eu)

beginnerNote: The DCT removes stalling and clutch anxiety, but 248 kg and litre-class torque make it an intimidating and expensive first bike.
whoFor: Distance riders and commuters who want a genuine two-up tourer with the effortless convenience of Honda's automatic DCT gearbox.
notFor: Maybe not for you if you want a light, sporty machine or any off-road ability - this is a committed road tourer.
about: The NT1100 is Europe's best-selling sport-tourer, built around the Africa Twin's 1,084cc parallel twin and Honda's six-speed dual-clutch transmission, which shifts automatically or via bar-mounted paddles with no clutch lever. The 2025 facelift brought a sharper fairing with DRLs, a six-axis IMU with cornering ABS, more mid-range torque and an optional Showa EERA electronically adjusted suspension version. With a 20.4 L tank, adjustable screen, cruise control and Apple CarPlay/Android Auto on a 6.5-inch touchscreen, it is a consummate all-weather mile-eater.
pros: Smooth, proven DCT automatic ideal for touring and traffic
Excellent two-up comfort with big grabrails and pannier options
20.4 L tank plus 5.0 L/100km gives ~400 km range
Strong equipment: cruise, CarPlay/Android Auto, adjustable screen, cornering ABS
Torque-rich 1,084cc twin retuned for 2025
cons: 248 kg kerb weight (DCT) is a lot at parking speeds
Chain final drive needs maintenance on a dedicated tourer
DCT adds ~EUR 1,100 over the manual version
sources: Honda Motor Europe 25YM NT1100 & NT1100 Electronic Suspension press kit technical specifications (hondanews.eu)
